title: Photo 202 · 콜로설 · 청자 상감 · 무릎 꿇기 옆 (양 무릎) · 북유럽 30대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Scandinavian woman in her late 30s, very fair skin tone with cool pink undertones and faint freckling across the shoulders, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, waist-length straight hair swept behind her shoulders, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears long teardrop earrings and has sharp stiletto nails.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so deep from front to back that her belly reaches beyond one edge of the frame and her rear beyond the other. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it drops, settles and presses down onto the thighs beneath it.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Korean celadon inlay style — a soft pale jade-green glaze ground inlaid with deep indigo and black slip cranes, clouds and chrysanthemum medallions, a fine dark double-line band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs like contour lines, inlaid medallions filling the space between every band. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Kneeling upright on the platform seen from directly to her side, both calves folded beneath her thighs and her rear settled back onto her heels, her back straight, her near hand resting on her thigh and her far arm held back so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head turned toward the camera, the whole depth of her body read from the side, full body head to knees filling the frame.

Footwear: Extreme pale jade-green platform stiletto sandals with a single ankle strap, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the pale glaze staying pale and the inlaid motifs crisp, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide.
